doc.title: Oliver Nelson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 10, 2020

title: Leonard Feather's book, taxidermy and model railroads
summary: His father's varied interests: taxidermy, undertaking, model trains tied to his Pullman porter father, and tinkering.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Okay. I just wanted to tell you that I don’t know if you know that your father made the 1960 edition of Leonard Feather’s book.
Oh yeah. Leonard Feather loved my dad, man.
It mentions that he was a cab driver and studied taxidermy perhaps?

Yup. He studied taxidermy for a while and thought about going into the undertaking business. And actually he wanted to get his pilot’s license. He never did that, but he had a lot of interests. But one of the big things he did for leisure was model railroading. He would build elaborate train layouts. He actually built one for me personally and I didn’t take care of it very well, but he had the mountains and all that stuff, went to Japan and bought brass engines and brought them back, and he was really — because his father was a Pullman porter on the railroad. So trains had always been a part of his life and he loved model railroads. So he was a tinkerer. He could take your timing belt out of your car and fix that if it needed to be done, just a really, really interesting guy.
